Let me analyze M1 carefully. Graph: e0=0→1 (a), e1=1→3 (b), e2=0→2 (c), e3=2→3 (d). drop_ping=[3] — edge 3 = (2,3) is LOST, not edge 2!

I wrote "drop_ping=(3,)" — the PING on edge 3 (from node 2 to node 3) is lost. So:
- t=0: source allocates; transmits e0 (arrives node 1 at 1), e2 (arrives node 2 at 1).
- t=1: node 1 allocates; transmits e1 → node 3 at 2. Node 2 allocates; transmits e3 → LOST (dropped) → no delivery.
- t=2: node 3 (dest) allocates via e1 → finalize complete=true → ACK on e1 → arrives node 1 at 3.
- t=3: node 1 credits e1 → finalize complete=true, proof {1} → ACK on e0 → arrives node 0 at 4.
- t=4: node 0 credits e0 → proof {0,1}; e2 not credited (node 2 never got credit for e3 — its PING was lost so node 2 never finalized... wait node 2 has no credits at all) → no finalize yet.
- t=100: deadline: node 2 unfinalized → finalize complete=false, proof {} → ACK to parent e2 → arrives node 0 at 101. Source (node 0) unfinalized → finalize complete=false at t=100 with proof {0,1} ✓ (implementation gives source_proof [0,1] ✓ and final 100, host delivery 101 ✓).
- t=101: release at 101 (prio 1) → frees all 4 entries; then ACK on e2 arrives at node 0 → absent → ignored_ack=1 ✓ implementation.

So metrics: allocations=4, cache_peak [1,1,1,1], peak 4, network_ack_tx=3 (node3→e1, node1→e0, node2timeout→e2), ignored_ack=1, late_ping=0 ✓ implementation right; my expectation mislabeled the drop (I thought edge 2 was dropped).
